title: Maximum-coordinate coherent prisms agree with right pinch
statement:
Use the coherent nerve of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], the right mapping identification $\Phi$ of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-pinched-adjunction], the pinched resolution $Q^\bullet$ of [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution], and its maximum map $q^n:Q^n\to\Delta^n$ of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. Let $A$ be a small locally Kan simplicial category, $x,y$ objects (possibly equal), $P=N_{\mathrm{hc}}A$ and $T=A(x,y)$. Write $U_P(x,y)$ and $j:\operatorname{Map}^R_P(x,y)\to U_P(x,y)$ for the arrow mapping space and right-pinch map of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison].

For $a:\Delta^n\to T$, specify a prism $f(a):\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\to P$ by the following coherent-simplex data on each chain $(\epsilon_0,b_0)\leq\cdots\leq(\epsilon_r,b_r)$ in $[1]\times[n]$. Its object at position $k$ is $x$ for $\epsilon_k=0$, and $y$ for $\epsilon_k=1$. On a mapping subset-poset for $i\leq j$ with $\epsilon_i=0,\epsilon_j=1$, the morphism map is the composite of $a$ with the nerve of the monotone function
$$S\longmapsto\max\{b_k:k\in S,\ \epsilon_k=0\},\qquad \{i,j\}\subseteq S\subseteq\{i,\ldots,j\}.$$
For $\epsilon_i=\epsilon_j$ it is constant at the identity of the corresponding object. These data define prisms constant at $x,y$ on their two ends, compatible with all simplicial operators, and hence a map $f:T\to U_P(x,y)$ (interchange the two prism factors for the internal-functor convention). Define $\tau:T\to\operatorname{Sing}_QT$ by $\tau_n(a)=a q^n$. Then the following equality holds as simplicial maps, naturally under simplicial functors of $A$:
$$f=j\,\Phi_{A,x,y}^{-1}\tau.$$

source.place: Arakawa, Levelwise nerves of simplicial categories, Remark 2.5, printed p.34, and the fiber comparison in Proposition 3.2, printed pp.35-36. Equality with the right-pinch map is an agent-explicit refinement using the maximum map of HTT Section 2.2.2, printed p.76. No Stacks tag states this identity; read online, archive WANTED.

proof.text: Fix n and a: Δ^n→T. The coherent nerve identifies a simplex with an enriched functor from the subset-poset realization. For a chain in [1]×[n], use the displayed object assignments and maximum formula. Its indexing set is nonempty because it contains the initial endpoint i. Inclusion of subsets increases the maximum. Check composition at an intermediate index k: if its ε-coordinate is 0, the second subset contains k, and every zero-coordinate entry in the first subset has b-coordinate at most b_k, so adjoining the first subset leaves the maximum of the second unchanged. If its ε-coordinate is 1, the second subset adds no zero-coordinate entries, so the maximum of the first is unchanged. These are exactly composition with an identity in A. For pairs with equal ε all maps are identities, including i=j. A monotone operator on the chain acts by direct image of subsets and preserves this maximum; repeated vertices cause no change. Thus these enriched functors give compatible coherent simplices, constant on both end faces, and define the prism f(a).

source.place: Remark 2.5, printed p.34: coherent-simplex description and naturality

proof.text: For a monotone α:[m]→[n], the direct-image description of Q and its maximum map gives q^n Q(α)=α q^m, since max α(I)=α(max I) for every nonempty I. Thus τ_n(a)=a q^n defines a simplicial map T→Sing_Q T. Set z=Φ^{-1}(τ_n(a)). The pinched-adjunction statement says precisely that z is a map J^n→P whose enriched adjoint has the specified object images x,y and mapping map a q^n:Q^n→A(x,y). On Δ^{n+1}, this simplex is constant on the entire initial face. At this point z is a pinched simplex, before applying the right-pinch map.

source.place: Proposition 3.2, printed pp.35-36, together with the maximum-map calculation of HTT §2.2.2, printed p.76

proof.text: The stated definition of j precomposes z with h:Δ^1×Δ^n→Δ^{n+1}, where h(0,b)=b and h(1,b)=n+1. Fix a chain and a subset S between a 0-endpoint i and a 1-endpoint j. Direct image under h sends S to I(S)∪{n+1}, where I(S)={b_k:k∈S, ε_k=0} is nonempty. Its mapping element in Q^n is represented by I(S) in the canonical subset quotient. Explicitly, if the initial endpoint b_i is not 0, prepend the edge from 0 to b_i; the initial face is collapsed, so this edge maps to the identity, and subset composition changes the representative to {0}∪I(S) without changing its image. The cubical quotient identifies these representatives on the subcube with coordinate b_i equal to 1. The maximum map therefore sends this class to max I(S). This calculation applies to every inclusion chain of subsets, hence to every simplex of each mapping nerve. Applying the mapping map a q^n gives exactly the nerve of S↦max I(S), followed by a. Pairs with equal ε lie in an end face and give identities. Consequently j(z) has precisely the coherent-simplex data of f(a).

source.place: Proposition 4.6.5.10 and Construction 4.6.5.7, right-pinch map; explicit subset evaluation is the agent refinement

proof.text: For a simplex operator α:[m]→[n], the maximum formula commutes with α by max α(I)=α(max I), so f(a) restricts to f(aα). For a simplicial functor F:A→A', postcomposing a with F on mapping sets commutes with this formula and carries each identity to the corresponding identity. The naturality of Φ and j gives the same compatibilities on j Φ^{-1}τ. The equality proved for every n and a therefore is an equality of simplicial maps f=j Φ^{-1}τ, natural in A and the displayed endpoints.
